content.title: Moya Brennan: ‘First Lady of Celtic Music’ dies aged 73 | The Independent
content.text: Stay up to date with notifications from The IndependentNotifications can be managed in browser preferences.Not nowYes pleaseSwipe for next articleAllNewsSportCultureLifestyle‘First Lady of Celtic Music’ dies aged 73Copy linkBookmark popoverRemoved from bookmarksClose popoverNoel Duggan, Ciaran Brennan, Moya Brennan, Padraig Duggan and Paul Brennan in 1982 (Getty)Moya Brennan, the lead singer of the acclaimed Irish folk band Clannad, has died at the age of 73. Often referred to as the “First Lady of Celtic Music”, she passed away peacefully on Monday, 13 April, having been diagnosed with pulmonary fibrosis in 2020. Brennan co-founded Clannad in 1970 with her brothers and uncles, serving as the band's lead vocalist for over 50 years. Clannad achieved significant international success, winning a Bafta for their work on Robin of Sherwood and a Grammy Award for their 1999 album Landmarks. Beyond her work with Clannad, Brennan had a successful solo career, collaborated with notable artists, and is widely credited with introducing the Irish language to mainstream music.
